newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to up, pork bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to up, pork bellies mixed.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent a lb higher while early calls on pork belly futures ranged mixed at 0.300 cent lower to 0.300 higher, livestock analysts said.

Steady to $1.00 per cwt higher cash hog indications and further strength in cash pork values on firm demand should spark early buying in hog futures. Hog marketings have been running lighter than anticipated, partly due to cold weather, analysts said.
Nearby lean contracts also appeared oversold Tuesday, especially with the lean carcass index advancing, they said.
Some analysts were still uncertain if packers were cutting back on slaughter operations due to profit margins because hog supplies are tight. This could again bring uneven trade, they said.

Some analysts expect early pressure in pork belly futures following Tuesday's CME out-of-town report. The CME reported net storings last week in CME-approved warehouses outside Chicago at 2.83 million lbs, above expectations for 1.5 million to 2.0 million lbs net in-movement. This should weigh on futures, they said.

However, others noted that storings were still running below year-ago levels when the net in-movement during the corresponding week was 3.715 million lbs. The much-lighter-than-expected pace of slaughter recently and mostly firm tone to cash bellies should also lend support.
Cash bellies weighing 12 to 14 lbs sold Tuesday steady to $2.00 per cwt lower but bellies weighing 14 to 16 lbs sold steady to $1.00 higher, USDA said.
USDA estimated week-to-date slaughter through Tuesday at 681,000 head, well behind 712,000 in the same period a week ago and 708,000 a year ago.
